Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with the workspace contract in `README.md`. Then I’ll inspect the current rollout evidence and use the required fish-control bookshelf protocol; I’ll also use the wake-visual inspection skill because this policy change depends on interpreting both 3D views.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis and forbids local CFD. I’m now reading the inherited control guidance and both applicable skill contracts in full before inspecting the sampled trajectories.

The inherited bank shows a mature capture scaffold and repeated regressions from terminal slip/crossflow cancellation. The current evidence must decide whether this iteration should add a mechanism or deliberately simplify/restore one, so I’m inventorying all four sampled policies, their inherited notes, metrics, diagnostics, and visual sheets before touching the candidate.

All four samples are valid direct-uniform captures, so there is no semantic failure in this batch. I’ll compare the strongest scalar capture (`cd24…`) against the lowest-scoring, tightest-threshold capture (`d00…`) as the most informative regression, then check the other two for whether the visible pattern is consistent. This is the visual-skill comparison boundary for this batch.

The visual sheets show the same qualitative class across all four: self-propelled motion, alternating compact mid-plane vortices, coherent oblique structures, and a shallow final approach without collision or instability. I’m tightening that qualitative read against the compact aggregate metrics now; the large JSON embeds every trajectory sample, so I’m querying only the diagnostic summary fields and comparing the four policy implementations directly.

The quantitative cross-check supports the current prefill as the best progress mechanism, not the cleanest actuator mechanism: it reaches every 6–1L milestone earliest and has the best distance integral, while all variants still hit the hard joint-rate ceiling and spend about 17.3–17.4% of samples above 90% anterior rate. The posterior-work release shortens path and slightly lowers load but loses progress and increases terminal yaw. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a compact mechanism that can address that unresolved rate/contact issue without another scalar threshold or wake-cancellation residual.

The shelf’s C-start/closed-loop CPG invariant fits the evidence without importing species-specific timing: retain strong bounded curvature while the measured body-frame velocity course is unresolved, then remove only outward target-conditioned work as the course aligns, while preserving joint reversal and posterior traveling-wave structure. I’m recording that visual diagnosis, transfer block, and falsification criteria in the required notes before editing the policy.

The candidate now implements exactly one additional mechanism: course-resolved, joint-local relief of outward steering work. It leaves the prefill’s propulsion, target geometry, response handoff, carrier guard, and all unresolved-course steering unchanged. I’m now distilling the sampled four-way comparison into the reusable guidance bank; this records prior evidence only, not an unevaluated claim about the new candidate.

Both required provenance files are updated. I’m moving to deterministic validation now: parameter-schema consistency, policy syntax/contract checks, single-candidate scope, and the mandated check-runner. I will not run CFD.

The workspace’s mandated `check-runner` is itself an agent contract, so I’m invoking that checker now to run the three prescribed non-CFD validations and report PASS/FAIL. While it runs, I’ll review only the candidate-specific diff and mathematical edge cases, avoiding duplicate formal checks.

The mandated checker passed the guidance and boundary checks. Its policy-contract command failed only because `julia` is absent from the current `PATH`, not because of the candidate. I’m resolving whether a workspace/toolchain Julia binary is available and will rerun the checker with that executable if present; the workspace requires repairing and rerunning any failed check.

A validated evaluator runtime exists at `julia`; it was simply omitted from `PATH`. I’m rerunning the mandated checker with that directory prepended so the prescribed contract command executes unchanged.

Produced one Phase 2 candidate: `dogfish3d_course_resolved_total_work_guard_v1`.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [Evidence and bookshelf transfer notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable control lesson](guidance/control_experience.md:111)

The candidate adds course-resolved, joint-local relief of outward steering work while preserving unresolved-course steering, carrier reversal, and the existing capture scaffold.

All mandated checks passed: material guidance update, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary validation. No CFD was run.
